Frames the punchy syncopated single-note hook played across the D and G strings

keyAndScale.modalCharacter: Infectious 80s dance-rock funk built on tight Dorian syncopation and dry single-coil Stratocaster cutting power
keyAndScale.relativeMinor: Eb major is the relative major

sectionProgressions.description: Iconic syncopated single-note groove with crisp palm muting and rhythmic space
Staccato upper-register triad stabs on the D, G, and B strings with muted 16th-note chucks

harmonicFunction: Cm7 (i7) - Heavy funk tonic groove anchoring the entire track
Bb (♭VII) - Subtonic chord providing classic modal forward momentum
F (IV) - The major IV chord carrying the natural A note, defining the C Dorian sound

techniques.name: 16th-Note Funk Chucking & Rhythmic Rest Control
techniques.description: Precise right-hand continuous 16th-note pendulum picking combined with fretting-hand mutes to create a laser-tight groove with deliberate silences.

notes: Single-note hook: 10th fret D string (C root) to 8th fret (Bb) and 10th fret G string (F)
Triad stabs on strings 2, 3, and 4 (Cm7 at fret 8, Bb at fret 6, F at fret 10)
Complete rhythmic rests on beats 2 and 4
sequence: Lock your right hand into constant 16th-note motion
Squeeze your fretting fingers for the note duration and instantly relax for the muted clicks
Honor every rest—the silence between notes is what makes this riff groove
tips: Use middle or bridge single-coil pickup for maximum percussive bite
Keep compressor attack fast and compression moderate to even out pick attack
Practice with a metronome focusing strictly on locking with the snare on 2 and 4

techniques.name: Interlocking Minimalist Dual-Guitar Layering
techniques.description: The production signature of Kick, where Tim Farriss's syncopated single-note baseline interacts with Kirk Pengilly's upper-register triad chops, leaving massive sonic space for Michael Hutchence's vocals and Garry Gary Beers's bass.

notes: C Dorian scale tones: C - D - Eb - F - G - A - Bb
Fret 8 upper triad stabs (Eb, G, C) on strings 2, 3, and 4
Strict separation between the single-note groove and chord accents
Dry gate reverb and sharp pickup dynamics
sequence: Establish the steady single-note syncopation on string 4
Layer the staccato triad stab precisely on the syncopated offbeats
Drop out completely during vocal breaths to intensify dynamics
Dig in on the F major triad to accentuate the Dorian major 6th (A natural)
tips: Recorded directly into the desk and through a Roland JC-120 by producer Chris Thomas
Do not play full 6-string barres—the essence of this track is ruthless minimalism
Keep your picking wrist loose but your fretting-hand muting razor-sharp

sections.name: Intro Drum Loop & Single-Note Riff Hook
sections.description: Andrew Farriss and Tim Farriss's world-famous syncopated single-note guitar hook that opens the track.
notes: Mute slightly with your palm for tight articulation
Do not rush the syncopated offbeats
Leave wide open silence on the downbeats

sections.name: Verse 1 Minimalist Funk Stabs
sections.description: Upper-register chord stabs entering behind Michael Hutchence's seductive, whisper-close vocal delivery.
notes: Use compact 3-string triads on the D, G, and B strings
Kill the sound instantly after each stab with fretting hand release
Keep the right-hand wrist relaxed in steady 16th motion

sections.name: Pre-Chorus Build & Rhythmic Tension
sections.description: The building pre-chorus ('All you got is this moment, the twenty-first century's yesterday...') increasing rhythmic pressure.
notes: Lock into Garry Gary Beers's walking bassline
Let the chord stabs ring slightly longer before clamping down
Prepare for the explosive entrance of the chorus hook

sections.name: Chorus Groove ('I Need You Tonight')
sections.description: The global #1 chorus hook combining the driving single-note syncopation with upper triad Dorian stabs.
notes: Accentuate beat 1 on the Cm7 stab
Highlight the bright A natural note in the F major triad (10th fret strings 2-4)
Maintain laser-sharp dance pocket at 109 BPM

sections.name: Instrumental Guitar Break & Funk Lead
sections.technique: C Dorian Single-Note Funk Lead & Biting Attack
sections.description: Kirk Pengilly and Tim Farriss's syncopated guitar break cutting through the mix with funky single-coil snap and Dorian fills.
notes: Staccato single-note phrasing across frets 8 to 12
Emphasize the syncopated 16th-note pickups
Crisp pick attack using the bridge single-coil

sections.name: Outro Dance Climax & Transition to Mediate
sections.description: The hypnotic final groove where the guitars lock in with saxophone jabs before seamlessly transitioning into 'Mediate'.
notes: Interlock the single-note root motif with staccato chords
Hold the unwavering 109 BPM tempo right to the final drum hit
Keep muting crystal clean with no extraneous string vibrations

guitar.recommended: 1956 Fender Stratocaster or G&L ASAT Classic
guitar.pickup: Bridge or middle single-coil for clean cutting presence

amp.recommended: Roland JC-120 Jazz Chorus & Fender Twin Reverb

effects.compressor: Boss CS-3 or MXR Dyna Comp (essential for funk punch)

beginner.title: Single-Note Hook Notes
steps: Find the notes on the 4th (D) string: frets 10 (C) and 8 (Bb)
Practice the four-note pattern slowly at 80 BPM
Focus on stopping the sound immediately with fretting fingers

intermediate.title: 16th-Note Funk Pocket
steps: Combine the single-note hook with upper triad chord stabs
Lock tightly with the 109 BPM drum loop without dragging

advanced.title: Studio Precision & Dynamic Rest
steps: Play both rhythm parts (single-note and triads) seamlessly
Replicate the exact attack, compression, and gating of the Kick album tone
Perform live with zero string noise during the rests

commonMistakes: Letting open strings ring during the silent rests
Rushing ahead of the 109 BPM dance tempo
Using too much amplifier distortion instead of ultra-clean compressed bite
practiceRoutine: 5 minutes: Single-note hook articulation at 85 BPM → 109 BPM
5 minutes: 16th-note muted chucking and triad stabs
5 minutes: Metronome practice with clicks on beats 2 and 4 only
metronomeWork: Practice with a 16th-note subdivided click at 90 BPM
Advance to standard quarter-note click at 109 BPM
